drift: Drift Protocol is one of the largest decentralized exchanges on Solana, offering perpetual futures, spot trading, lending and borrowing in one app. DRIFT is its governance token, used to vote on how the protocol is run.
drv: Derive (formerly Lyra) is a decentralized protocol for options, perpetual futures and structured products, running on its own Derive Chain built on the OP Stack. DRV is the governance token: holders steer the protocol and receive a share of fee revenue.
dte-de: Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecom company, based in Bonn, and the former state postal and telephone network of Germany. It provides mobile and internet services in Germany and across Europe and controls the US operator T-Mobile US.
dual: Dual is a tokenization engine for real-world assets that lets businesses build programmable tokens for anything from currencies and loyalty points to real estate, treasuries and physical products. DUAL is the utility token that powers the ecosystem.
duk: Duke Energy is one of the largest US utilities, based in Charlotte, North Carolina. It generates and delivers electricity to millions of customers in the Carolinas, Florida and the Midwest, sells natural gas, and runs a large nuclear fleet.
dusk: Dusk (DUSK) is a layer-1 blockchain from the Netherlands built for regulated financial markets. It lets tokenized securities be issued and traded in line with EU law while protecting privacy; DUSK is used for fees and staking.
dydx: dYdX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures, founded in 2017 by former Coinbase engineer Antonio Juliano. It now runs on its own blockchain in the Cosmos ecosystem; the DYDX token is used for staking, network security and governance.
dym: Dymension is a modular layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK that makes it easy to launch custom rollups called RollApps. It gives them shared security, liquidity and interoperability, and DYM is used for staking, fees and governance.
ecl: Ecolab is a US company based in Saint Paul, Minnesota, founded in 1923, that provides water treatment, cleaning, hygiene and infection-prevention products and services. Its customers include restaurants, hotels, hospitals, food plants and factories; it also owns Nalco Water.
eden: OpenEden is a Singapore-based real-world asset tokenization platform that issues TBILL, a token backed by short-term US Treasury bills. It has also launched the USDO stablecoin; EDEN is the ecosystem token.
edu: Open Campus (EDU) is a protocol building blockchain infrastructure for education: digital diplomas and certificates and funding for educational content. The project is backed by Animoca Brands and runs its own network, EDU Chain.
eem: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets (EEM) is a BlackRock ETF holding large companies from emerging markets, including China, India and Taiwan.
efa: iShares MSCI EAFE (EFA) invests in large companies from Europe, Australasia and the Far East, excluding the US and Canada.
egl1: EGL1 is a meme token built around a bald eagle and American patriotic imagery that calls itself the first superhero meme. It has no practical use beyond its community and trades as a memecoin.
egld: MultiversX (formerly Elrond) is a layer-1 blockchain from Romania that uses sharding for high throughput. Launched in 2020, it supports smart contracts and DeFi; EGLD pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
eigen: EigenCloud (formerly EigenLayer) is a restaking protocol on Ethereum: staked ETH is reused to secure other services and networks. The project was founded by Sreeram Kannan, and the EIGEN token is used for governance and to back guarantees for its verifiable cloud services.
el-fr: EssilorLuxottica is a French-Italian eyewear giant formed in 2018 by the merger of Essilor and Luxottica. It makes spectacle lenses, frames and sunglasses under brands like Ray-Ban and Oakley, runs optical chains such as Sunglass Hut and makes smart glasses with Meta.
el-token: ELYSIA is a peer-to-peer real-estate investment platform that tokenises properties so many people can co-invest in a building with small amounts and connects sellers with buyers. EL is the platform's token used within its ecosystem.
ela: Elastos is a blockchain platform founded by operating-system veteran Rong Chen to build a user-owned "SmartWeb". Its main chain is merge-mined with Bitcoin, borrowing Bitcoin's hash power for security, and ELA pays for transactions and services in the ecosystem.
elephant: Elephant Money is a DeFi protocol on BNB Chain built around the ELEPHANT token and its TRUNK stablecoin. Its treasury and token mechanics are meant to fund yield for users holding and staking these tokens.
elf: aelf (ELF) is a layer-1 blockchain from Singapore, launched in 2017, built with a main chain and side chains for scaling. Smart contracts are written in C#, and the project focuses on AI tools for developers.
elsa: HeyElsa is an AI platform that turns plain-language requests into on-chain actions: swaps, bridges, staking, yield search and portfolio management across many networks. It offers an AI copilot for users and widgets, an SDK and APIs for businesses.
elv: Elevance Health (Anthem until 2022) is one of the largest US health insurers, based in Indianapolis. It sells health plans under the Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield brand, serves Medicare and Medicaid programs and runs the CarelonRx pharmacy business.
emr: Emerson Electric is a US industrial technology company based in St. Louis, Missouri, founded in 1890. It makes automation systems, control valves, measurement instruments and industrial software used by factories, refineries, chemical and power plants.
ena: Ethena is an Ethereum protocol that issues USDe, a synthetic dollar kept stable by crypto collateral and hedging with futures. ENA is the protocol's governance token; the project was founded by Guy Young.
enb: Enbridge is a Canadian energy company from Calgary that runs one of North America's largest networks of oil and gas pipelines. It also supplies natural gas to homes in Ontario and develops wind and solar power.
enel: Enel is Italy's largest energy company, based in Rome and founded in 1962 as the state power monopoly. It generates electricity, including renewables through Enel Green Power, owns power grids and sells electricity and gas in Italy, Spain (Endesa) and Latin America.
eni: Eni is an Italian energy company based in Rome, founded in 1953 by Enrico Mattei. It produces oil and gas in dozens of countries, especially in Africa, refines fuel, sells gas and electricity through Plenitude and is growing renewable energy and biofuels.
enj: Enjin Coin (ENJ) is the token of the Enjin ecosystem, which has been building infrastructure for in-game NFT items since 2017. Developers issue in-game objects on Enjin's own blockchain, and ENJ is used to create them, pay fees and stake.
enr: Siemens Energy is a German energy equipment maker based in Munich, spun off from Siemens in 2020. It builds gas turbines, power grid equipment and transformers, and wind turbines through Siemens Gamesa.
ens: Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is a domain name system on Ethereum that replaces long wallet addresses with readable names like name.eth. The service launched in 2017 under Nick Johnson; ENS is the governance token of its DAO.
enso: Enso is a network that brings different blockchains together in one access point for developers: its API and tools let them read data and build and execute transactions with DeFi protocols across many chains. ENSO is the network token.
eog: EOG Resources is a US oil and gas producer based in Houston, formerly Enron Oil & Gas, which split from Enron in 1999. It extracts oil and natural gas mainly from shale fields in Texas and other US states.
epic: Epic Cash (EPIC) is private digital cash built on the MimbleWimble protocol, which hides transaction amounts and participants. The coin is created by mining and had no pre-allocation to its founders.
epol: iShares MSCI Poland (EPOL) invests in Poland's largest listed companies: banks, energy firms and retailers.
eqix: Equinix is the world's largest colocation data center operator, based in Redwood City, California, and founded in 1998. It rents server space in dozens of major cities and links the networks of cloud providers, banks and telecoms; it is structured as a REIT.
era: Caldera is a rollup-as-a-service platform that helps projects launch their own layer-2 chains on Ethereum, plus Metalayer to connect them. ERA is the token for staking, payments and governance.
erg: Ergo is a proof-of-work blockchain launched in 2019 with the eUTXO model and powerful smart contracts for DeFi and financial tools. ERG is mined, and the network is known for its focus on decentralization with no pre-mine.
esp: Espresso (ESP) is a transaction-confirmation network for layer-2 blockchains based on BFT consensus. It gives rollups a near-instant, reliable view of each other's state, making interaction between chains easier and protecting against block reorgs.
etc: Ethereum Classic is the original Ethereum chain that kept running after the 2016 hard fork, when most of the community reversed the effects of The DAO hack. ETC sticks to the "code is law" principle and, unlike Ethereum, still uses Proof of Work mining.
eth: Ether (ETH) is the coin of Ethereum, the biggest smart-contract platform, which hosts DeFi, NFTs and stablecoins. Ether pays the network's transaction fees; Ethereum was co-founded by Vitalik Buterin in 2015.
etha: iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) is BlackRock's spot ether ETF, launched in 2024, giving brokerage-account access to ETH, the coin of the Ethereum network.
ethfi: Ether.fi is a liquid restaking protocol on Ethereum that is also growing into a crypto neobank with a card for spending and saving. Users stake ETH and keep it liquid through the eETH token; ETHFI is the governance token.
ethw: EthereumPoW (ETHW) is a fork of Ethereum created in September 2022, when the main network switched from mining to proof of stake. Some miners kept running the old proof-of-work chain, and ETHW is its native coin.
etn: Eaton is a power management company legally domiciled in Dublin, with roots going back to 1911 in the United States. It makes electrical equipment for buildings, data centers and utility grids, as well as components for aircraft and vehicles.
etn-token: Electroneum is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain with transactions in a few seconds and instant finality. Founded in the UK by Richard Ells, the project targets mobile users and payments in developing countries; ETN is its native coin.
eul: Euler is a DeFi lending protocol on Ethereum where users supply and borrow crypto assets. Its second version lets anyone create their own lending markets with custom risk settings; EUL is the governance token.
eurc: EURC is a euro-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle, the company behind USDC. Each token is backed one-to-one by euro reserves, it is issued under the EU's MiCA rules, and it runs on Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Base and other blockchains.
eurcv: EUR CoinVertible (EURCV) is a euro stablecoin issued by SG-FORGE, the digital-assets subsidiary of French bank Société Générale. Each token aims to equal one euro and is backed by reserves; it runs on public blockchains such as Ethereum.
eure: EURe is a euro stablecoin issued by Monerium, a licensed electronic money institution from Iceland. Each token is regulated e-money backed one-to-one by euros and can move on Ethereum, Gnosis, Polygon and other networks or be redeemed via a bank IBAN.
europ: EURØP is a euro stablecoin compliant with the EU's MiCA rules, issued by a licensed French issuer supervised by the regulator ACPR. Each token is backed 1:1 by euros held at EU banks such as Société Générale and can be redeemed for euros.
eurs: STASIS EURO (EURS) is a euro stablecoin issued by STASIS, a company based in Malta. Each token is meant to be backed one-to-one by euro reserves, with regular audits, and it is used to hold and move euros on blockchains such as Ethereum.
ev: Everything (EV) is a project that combines several DeFi protocols into one interconnected ecosystem. The EV token is used for governance, for using the services and for capturing value across all of the project's products.
evaa: EVAA Protocol is a decentralized lending protocol on the TON network. Users can supply crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral, including directly from Telegram; EVAA is the protocol's governance token.
ewg: iShares MSCI Germany (EWG) invests in large German companies such as SAP, Siemens, Allianz and Deutsche Telekom.
ewt: Energy Web Token (EWT) is the native token of Energy Web Chain, an open blockchain for the energy sector from the non-profit Energy Web. Energy companies use it to track renewable power and certificates and to manage distributed devices.
f-token: SynFutures is a decentralized protocol for perpetual futures that lets users trade any asset and create new futures markets in seconds. Its V3 oAMM model combines an automated market maker with an on-chain order book; F is the protocol token.
fai: Freysa is an AI agent on the Base network, known for a game in which people paid to try to convince it to hand over a prize pool. The project builds autonomous AI agents that manage funds on their own; FAI is the ecosystem token.
fartcoin: Fartcoin (FARTCOIN) is a meme coin on Solana that appeared in late 2024 out of jokes around the AI agent Truth Terminal. The token has no practical use and exists as an internet joke, so its price depends on community interest.
fast-retailing: Fast Retailing is a Japanese company from Yamaguchi that owns Uniqlo, Asia's largest clothing chain. It also runs the GU, Theory and Comptoir des Cotonniers brands; founder Tadashi Yanai turned a family shop into a global retailer of basic clothing.
fbtc: Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) is Fidelity's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024, which holds real bitcoin in Fidelity's own custody.
fcx: Freeport-McMoRan is a US mining company based in Phoenix, Arizona, and one of the world's largest copper producers. It runs Indonesia's Grasberg mine, one of the biggest copper and gold deposits on Earth, plus mines in the US and Peru.
fdusd: First Digital USD (FDUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued since 2023 by First Digital Labs, part of Hong Kong-based First Digital Group. Each token is backed one-to-one by cash and short-term US Treasuries held in custody, and it is used mostly as a trading pair on major exchanges.
fdx: FedEx is a US logistics company based in Memphis, Tennessee, founded in 1971 by Frederick Smith. It runs one of the world's largest cargo airline fleets and delivers express parcels, freight and e-commerce shipments to more than 220 countries and territories.
fet: The Artificial Superintelligence Alliance (ASI) was formed in 2024 by merging the AI projects Fetch.ai, SingularityNET and Ocean Protocol. It builds decentralized infrastructure for artificial intelligence and autonomous agents; FET is the alliance's shared token.
ff: FF is the token of Falcon Finance, a "universal collateral" protocol: users deposit crypto or tokenized real-world assets and mint the synthetic dollar USDf against them. This gives liquidity without selling the assets; FF is used for governance and staking.
fida: Bonfida is a project in the Solana ecosystem known for the Solana Name Service, which lets people register readable .sol domains instead of long wallet addresses. FIDA is its governance token.
fil: Filecoin is a decentralized data storage network where anyone can rent out spare disk space and get paid in FIL. It was created by Juan Benet's company Protocol Labs, also known for the IPFS protocol, and its mainnet launched in 2020.
firo: Firo (formerly Zcoin) is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency launched in 2016. It uses its own protocols such as Lelantus Spark to hide the sender, receiver and amount of a transaction; FIRO is mined.
flip: Chainflip (FLIP) is a decentralized protocol for swapping native crypto assets between different blockchains, for example bitcoin for ETH, without wrapped tokens or bridges. Validators stake FLIP, and part of the fees is used to burn the token.
flock: FLock.io is a decentralized network for training and validating AI models, built by a team of researchers including Oxford alumni. Participants contribute compute and data and earn FLOCK for their part in training models.
floki: FLOKI is a memecoin launched in 2021 and named after Floki, Elon Musk's Shiba Inu dog. It has grown into a multi-chain token with its own ecosystem, including the Valhalla game, DeFi services and educational products.
flow: Flow (FLOW) is a layer-1 blockchain for consumer apps, created by Canadian studio Dapper Labs, the makers of CryptoKitties. NBA Top Shot and other digital collectibles run on it; FLOW is used for fees and staking.
flr: Flare is an Ethereum-compatible blockchain specialized in data: built-in oracles deliver prices and information from other networks and the internet. Its FAssets technology lets tokens without smart contracts, such as XRP, be used in DeFi.
fluid: Fluid is a DeFi protocol from the Instadapp team on Ethereum that combines lending and a decentralized exchange on shared liquidity, so collateral can work harder. The FLUID token replaced the former INST token and is used for governance.
flux: Flux is a decentralized cloud infrastructure where thousands of independent nodes provide computing power to run apps and websites. FLUX is mined and used to pay for services and to collateralize nodes.
fogo: Fogo is a layer-1 blockchain compatible with the Solana Virtual Machine, built on the Firedancer validator client and designed for on-chain trading, with very low latency and near-instant finality. FOGO is the network's native token for fees and staking.
fold: The Interfold is an open protocol for confidential shared computation: several parties add private data to a calculation without revealing it to each other. Uses include secret voting, sealed-bid auctions and confidential analytics; FOLD is the network token.
folks: Folks Finance (FOLKS) is a cross-chain DeFi lending protocol: users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral across different blockchains from a single interface. The project grew up in the Algorand ecosystem, and FOLKS is its governance token.
form: Four (FORM), formerly BinaryX, is the token of the ecosystem linked to Four.meme, a popular memecoin launchpad on BNB Chain. FORM is used for staking, rewards and taking part in ecosystem projects.
fort: Forta is a decentralized blockchain security monitoring network where bots analyze transactions in real time and warn about hacks, scams and anomalies. FORT is used to stake nodes and pay for services.
fp: Fren Pet is an on-chain virtual pet game on the Base network. Players buy and care for a digital pet with the FP token, keep it alive with items and can attack other pets to earn points and rewards.
ft: Flying Tulip is a DeFi project led by Andre Cronje, the creator of Yearn Finance, to build one on-chain exchange that combines spot trading, lending, perpetual futures and options. FT is its token; early buyers got an on-chain right to redeem it for their original contribution.
ftnt: Fortinet is a US cybersecurity company based in Sunnyvale, California, founded in 2000. It is best known for its FortiGate firewalls and FortiOS operating system, and sells network security, secure remote access and cloud protection to businesses and governments.
ftrb: Faith Tribe is a collaborative fashion platform where independent designers create, test and sell digital and physical clothing. The blockchain records design ownership, and the FTRB token is used for rewards, voting and payments in the ecosystem.
fun: FUNToken (FUN) is a token for online gaming and the iGaming industry, launched in 2017. It is used for bets, payments and rewards on gaming platforms, with transparent settlement on the blockchain.
fxnw: FastX Network (FXNW) is a decentralized artificial-intelligence infrastructure for Web3 applications. The project aims to connect AI services with blockchain apps, and the FXNW token is used for payments and participation in the network.
g-token: Gravity (G) is a layer-1 blockchain from Galxe, one of the largest platforms for Web3 quests and on-chain identity. The G token replaced the GAL token and is used for fees, staking and across Galxe services.
gal: GAL is the former token of Galxe, a Web3 rewards and digital-credentials platform where projects run campaigns to attract users. GAL has migrated to G, the token of Galxe's Gravity network, so old coins are exchanged for new ones.
gala: GALA is the token of Gala Games, a US blockchain gaming platform founded in 2019 by Eric Schiermeyer. It is used to buy in-game items and NFTs, reward network node operators and vote; Gala also runs music and film branches.
gas: Gas (GAS) is the second token of the NEO network, used to pay fees for transactions and running smart contracts. NEO holders automatically receive GAS as a reward, so the two coins work as a pair: NEO for governance, GAS as fuel.
gasoline: RBOB gasoline is the US futures contract for petrol. Its price depends on crude oil, the summer driving season and how busy refineries are.
gcoin: Playnance (GCOIN) is a blockchain ecosystem for online games, contests and prediction markets, built as a layer-3 network on Arbitrum. GCOIN is used in the platform's games, tournaments and DeFi features.
gd: General Dynamics is a US defense company from Reston, Virginia. It builds Gulfstream business jets, nuclear submarines, Abrams tanks and armored vehicles, and provides IT services to the US government.
ge: GE Aerospace is a US jet engine maker based in Cincinnati, the successor of the General Electric conglomerate founded in 1892 with Thomas Edison's involvement. After the 2024 split it focuses on engines for passenger and military aircraft and their servicing.
genius: Genius (GENIUS) is the token of Genius Terminal, an on-chain terminal for professional crypto trading with a focus on privacy. It combines swaps, cross-chain transfers and wallet management in one interface to make DeFi easier to use.
geod: GEODNET is a decentralized network of ground stations that receive navigation satellite signals (GPS and other GNSS) and provide corrections for centimeter-level positioning. Drones, farm machinery and robots use this data; station owners earn GEOD for running them.
gev: GE Vernova is an American energy company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, spun off from General Electric in 2024. It makes gas turbines, wind turbines, equipment for nuclear and hydro power, and technology for electricity grids.
ggbr: Goldfish Gold (GGBR) is a gold-backed token: each one represents 1/1000 of a troy ounce. The metal is held in a Wyoming trust as gold still in the ground at a deposit, not in bars, so the token gives on-chain access to that asset.
giga: Gigachad (GIGA) is a Solana meme coin inspired by the "Gigachad" internet meme about the ideal man with a chiselled jaw. It has no technical function and rests on its community and meme culture.
giggle: Giggle Fund (GIGGLE) is a BNB Chain meme token linked to Giggle Academy, an education initiative backed by Binance founder Changpeng Zhao. Part of the token's trading fees goes to donations for free education.
gild: Gilead Sciences is an American biopharmaceutical company based in California, founded in 1987. It is known for its HIV drugs (Biktarvy), hepatitis C treatments (Sovaldi, Harvoni) and the COVID-19 drug Veklury, and is expanding in cancer and inflammatory diseases.
gld: SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) is the biggest fund backed by physical gold: every share is backed by gold bars held in vaults.
glm: Golem (GLM) is one of the first decentralized computing projects, founded in Poland in 2016. Its network lets people rent out or rent computing power, for example for rendering and AI tasks; GLM is the payment token on Ethereum.
glmr: Moonbeam is an Ethereum-compatible smart contract network that runs as a parachain on Polkadot. It lets developers deploy Ethereum-style apps while connecting to other Polkadot chains, and GLMR pays fees, secures the network through staking and is used for governance.
glw: Corning is a US glass and materials maker from Corning, New York, founded in 1851. It is known for Gorilla Glass for smartphones and also makes optical fiber, display glass, ceramic filters for cars and lab glassware.
gmexicob: Grupo México is a Mexican conglomerate based in Mexico City and one of the world's largest copper producers through its subsidiary Southern Copper, with mines in Mexico and Peru. It also runs Ferromex, Mexico's largest railroad, and infrastructure businesses.
gmt: GMT is the governance token of STEPN, a move-to-earn app where users earn rewards for walking and running in NFT sneakers. The project was created by the Australian studio Find Satoshi Lab, and GMT is also used in its other products.
gmx: GMX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures and leveraged spot trading on Arbitrum and Avalanche. Traders trade straight from their wallets, liquidity providers earn a share of fees, and GMX is the governance and fee-sharing token.
gno: Gnosis is an ecosystem that began in 2015 as a prediction-market platform. It gave rise to the popular Safe multisig wallet, and today it develops the Gnosis Chain blockchain and payment services such as the Gnosis Pay card. GNO is used for staking and governance.
gnot: Gno.land is a layer-1 smart-contract platform developed by NewTendermint, the team of Cosmos co-founder Jae Kwon. Contracts are written in Gno, a deterministic, interpreted version of the Go language; GNOT is the network's token for fees and governance.
goat: Goatseus Maximus (GOAT) is a Solana memecoin launched in 2024 on pump.fun. It became famous because Truth Terminal, an experimental AI chatbot on X, kept promoting the joke behind it, making GOAT the first big 'AI agent' memecoin.
gods: Gods Unchained is a free-to-play digital trading card game by Immutable, where players truly own their cards as NFTs on Immutable's Ethereum layer-2 network. The GODS token is used to craft cards, trade and vote on the game's future.
gohome: GOHOME is a meme token born from a January 2025 incident on the White House website, when the words Go Home appeared on its page. The community turned the episode into a meme, and the token trades purely as a meme asset with no product behind it.
gold: Gold is the classic safe-haven asset that has served as a store of value for thousands of years. Central banks, jewellers and investors buy it, especially in times of crisis, inflation or war.
gomining: GoMining is a digital Bitcoin mining platform backed by real data centers: users buy virtual miners as NFTs and receive daily rewards in BTC. The GOMINING token is used to pay maintenance fees, get discounts and for staking.
goog: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, based in Mountain View, California. It earns mainly from search and YouTube advertising, plus Google Cloud, Android and subscriptions, and develops the Gemini AI and Waymo robotaxis. Class C shares (GOOG) carry no voting rights.
googl: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, based in Mountain View, California; Google was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin. It owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Google Cloud and the Gemini AI. Class A shares (GOOGL) carry voting rights.
googl-token: This is a Robinhood stock token that tracks Alphabet Class A shares, the parent company of Google, YouTube and Android. Robinhood launched such tokens in 2025 for customers in the European Union, letting them get US stock exposure on-chain around the clock.
gps: GoPlus Security (GPS) is a Web3 security network that checks tokens, smart contracts and addresses for scams and malicious activity. Its API is built into many wallets and exchanges; the GPS token is used to pay for security services.
gram: Gram (formerly Toncoin) is the native coin of the TON blockchain (The Open Network), originally conceived by Telegram's founders, the Durov brothers. The network is deeply integrated into Telegram, where the coin is used for transfers, fees, the built-in wallet and mini apps.
grass: Grass is a network where users share their unused internet bandwidth for rewards through a browser extension or app. This capacity helps collect public web data for training AI; the GRASS token runs on Solana.
griffain: Griffain is a project in the Solana ecosystem that lets users manage on-chain operations through AI agents: swapping tokens, providing liquidity and other DeFi actions. GRIFFAIN is the platform's token.
grnd: SuperWalk (GRND) is a South Korean move-to-earn app for walking and running. Users buy NFT sneakers to earn GRND tokens for moving at the right pace, while the basic mode lets them earn the WALK token without NFTs.
grt: The Graph is an indexing protocol for blockchain data, often called the "Google of blockchains": it organizes data from Ethereum and other networks so apps can query it quickly through open APIs called subgraphs. GRT pays for queries and is staked by indexers who run the network.
grvt: GRVT is a hybrid crypto exchange for perpetual futures built on ZKsync technology. It combines the speed of a centralized exchange with self-custody of assets and privacy; GRVT is the platform's token.
gs: Goldman Sachs is one of the world's best-known investment banks, founded in 1869 in New York. It advises on large mergers and acquisitions, arranges share offerings, trades securities and manages money for wealthy clients and institutions.
gt: GateToken (GT) is the native token of the Gate (Gate.io) crypto exchange, founded in 2013. It gives discounts on trading fees and access to new token launches, and it pays fees on the exchange's own blockchain network.
gtc: Gitcoin is a platform for funding open-source software and public goods in Web3, founded in 2017 by Kevin Owocki. It is known for grant rounds using quadratic funding; GTC is the governance token of Gitcoin DAO.
gwei: ETHGas (GWEI) is an Ethereum blockspace infrastructure protocol that splits space in blocks into tradable units. It lets users buy block space in advance and get fast transaction confirmations.
h: Humanity Protocol (H) is a blockchain that verifies that each user is a unique human through Proof of Humanity, including palm scans. Its goal is to protect Web3 services from bots and fake accounts, and the H token is used in the network.
hair: HairDAO is a decentralized science (DeSci) community that funds and runs research into hair loss treatments. Members use the HAIR token to govern the DAO and share in the results of its research and products.
handy: HANDY is a blockchain games and content platform that rewards users with virtual assets. Its main product HandyPick is a prediction game where users guess event outcomes and earn bonuses, while advertisers reach an audience from different countries.
hash: Provenance Blockchain is a public proof-of-stake layer-1 network built with the Cosmos SDK and launched in 2018, aimed at financial services such as loans, mortgages and fund administration. HASH is its native token for fees, staking and governance.
hbar: Hedera is a public network built on hashgraph technology, invented by Leemon Baird, for fast payments, tokenisation and enterprise apps. It is governed by a council of large companies including Google and IBM; HBAR pays fees and secures the network through staking.
hca: HCA Healthcare is the largest private hospital operator in the United States, based in Nashville, Tennessee, and founded in 1968. It runs hundreds of hospitals, surgery centers and urgent care clinics across the US and the UK.
hd: Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retail chain, founded in 1978 and based in Atlanta. It sells building materials, tools, garden equipment and household goods in the US, Canada and Mexico, serving both homeowners and professional builders.
hdfcbank: HDFC Bank is India's largest private-sector bank, based in Mumbai and founded in 1994. It offers retail and corporate banking, credit cards and loans, and in 2023 it merged with its parent, the mortgage lender HDFC.
heatoil: Heating oil is a refined oil product used for home heating and closely related to diesel fuel. Its price follows crude oil and winter demand.
hemi: Hemi is a modular blockchain protocol that joins Bitcoin and Ethereum into one "supernetwork"; one of its co-founders is early Bitcoin developer Jeff Garzik. Smart contracts on Hemi can see bitcoin data, and HEMI is used for staking and governance.
hez: Hermez Network was a zero-knowledge rollup that made cheap, fast token transfers on top of Ethereum. In 2021 the project joined Polygon, became Polygon Hermez (later Polygon zkEVM), and HEZ holders could swap their tokens for MATIC.
hitachi: Hitachi is a Japanese industrial and technology conglomerate based in Tokyo, founded in 1910. It develops digital IT solutions (Lumada), power equipment and electricity grids, railway systems and industrial automation.
hive: Hive is a blockchain that split from Steem in 2020 after the community rejected Justin Sun's takeover of Steemit. It rewards authors and readers for content, transactions on the network carry no fees, and it hosts the social network PeakD and the game Splinterlands.
hlt: Hilton Worldwide is a US hotel company based in McLean, Virginia, founded by Conrad Hilton in 1919. It manages and franchises thousands of hotels worldwide under brands such as Hilton, Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, DoubleTree and Hampton.
hmstr: Hamster Kombat is a tap-to-earn game in Telegram where players run a virtual crypto exchange as a hamster CEO. It became one of the most-played Telegram games in 2024; HMSTR is its token, distributed to players in an airdrop on the TON blockchain.
hnt: Helium (HNT) is a decentralized wireless network where people install hotspots and earn tokens for providing coverage. It first served IoT devices and now develops the Helium Mobile cellular service; since 2023 it has run on the Solana blockchain.
hogs: Lean hogs is a futures contract on the price of pork carcasses in the United States. It is driven by feed costs, exports to Asia and animal diseases.
hollar: HOLLAR (Hydrated Dollar) is a decentralized dollar stablecoin from Hydration, the DeFi network on Polkadot formerly known as HydraDX. Users mint HOLLAR by borrowing against crypto collateral in Hydration's money market.
holo: Holoworld (HOLO) is a platform for creating AI-agent virtual characters without coding: they can chat, livestream and interact with people across social networks. The project is developed by the studio Hologram Labs, and HOLO is the ecosystem token.
home: HOME is the token of DeFi App, an app that brings trading, swaps and yield across different blockchains into one interface without gas or complex setup. HOME holders take part in governance and get benefits on the platform.
hon-hai: Hon Hai Precision Industry, better known as Foxconn, is a Taiwanese company based in New Taipei, founded in 1974 by Terry Gou. It is the world's largest contract electronics maker, assembling iPhones and other devices for Apple and many brands, and builds AI servers.
honey: HONEY is the token of Hivemapper, a decentralized mapping network on Solana. Drivers mount Hivemapper dashcams in their cars to collect street-level imagery for a constantly updated world map and earn HONEY for their contributions, while companies pay to use the map data.
hopr: HOPR is a privacy protocol from Switzerland that runs a decentralized mixnet, hiding who is talking to whom when data moves across the internet. People who run HOPR nodes relay traffic and earn HOPR tokens for it.
hot: Holo (HOT) is the token of Holo, a project building hosting for apps on Holochain, a platform for distributed applications that does not use a classic blockchain. Computer owners can rent out space and processing power for hosting and earn rewards.
hsbc-holdings: HSBC is a British-Asian banking group headquartered in London, founded in 1865 in Hong Kong as the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. One of the world's largest banks, it earns most of its profit in Asia, especially Hong Kong.
hsk: HashKey Platform Token (HSK) is the ecosystem token of HashKey, a Hong Kong financial group that runs a licensed crypto exchange. It is used on the HashKey Chain network and to reward participants in the ecosystem.
ht: Huobi Token (HT) is the exchange token of Huobi, a crypto exchange founded in Beijing in 2013 by Leon Li that renamed itself HTX in 2023. The token gave discounts on trading fees and access to exchange services.
htx: HTX is the governance token of HTX DAO, the ecosystem around the HTX crypto exchange (formerly Huobi), which is linked to Justin Sun. Token holders vote on the project's development and get perks in the exchange's services.
huma: Huma Finance is a PayFi network that provides liquidity for payments and receivables financing on blockchain, notably on Solana. It lets users earn from real-world payment flows; HUMA is the governance token.
hunt: HUNT is the token of Hunt Town, a South Korean team of builders behind Steemhunt and the Mint Club token-creation platform. On Mint Club anyone can launch tokens priced by a bonding curve, often using HUNT as the reserve asset.
hwm: Howmet Aerospace is a US company based in Pittsburgh that makes engineered metal parts for aircraft engines and airframes, such as turbine blades, fasteners and structural components, plus forged aluminum wheels for trucks. It was spun out of Arconic, the former Alcoa, in 2020.
hype: Hyperliquid is its own layer-1 blockchain, best known for the decentralised exchange of the same name for perpetual futures and spot trading. HYPE is used for staking, fees and governance; the project is led by Jeff Yan.
hyper: Hyperlane is a permissionless interoperability protocol: anyone can connect their blockchain and send messages and tokens across dozens of networks. HYPER is the token for staking and governance.
iag-token: Iagon is a decentralized storage and computing platform built mainly on Cardano. People and businesses rent out spare disk space and processing power to the network, and the IAG token pays for these services and rewards providers.
ibe: Iberdrola is a Spanish energy company from Bilbao and one of the world's largest producers of wind and solar power. It owns power grids in Spain, the United Kingdom (ScottishPower), the United States (Avangrid) and Brazil (Neoenergia) and supplies electricity to millions of customers.
ibit: iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) is BlackRock's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024. It lets investors own bitcoin through a regular brokerage account without a crypto wallet.
ibkr: Interactive Brokers is a US online broker based in Greenwich, Connecticut, founded by Thomas Peterffy. It gives access to stocks, options, futures, currencies and bonds on hundreds of exchanges in dozens of countries and is known for low fees for active traders.
ibm: IBM is an American technology company based in Armonk, New York, founded in 1911. Once a leader in mainframes and personal computers, it now sells Red Hat hybrid cloud, enterprise software, the watsonx AI platform and consulting, and develops quantum computers.
icbc: ICBC (Industrial and Commercial Bank of China) is a state-owned Chinese bank based in Beijing and one of the largest banks in the world by assets. Founded in 1984, it serves hundreds of millions of customers and large companies; its H shares trade in Hong Kong.
icbc-cn: ICBC (A shares) are shares of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The state-owned Beijing bank, founded in 1984, is one of the world's largest and serves individuals, companies and the government through thousands of branches.
ice: Intercontinental Exchange is a US operator of exchanges and financial data based in Atlanta, founded in 2000 by Jeffrey Sprecher. It owns the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and the ICE futures exchanges, and provides mortgage technology and data services.
icicibank: ICICI Bank is one of India's largest private-sector banks, based in Mumbai and founded in 1994. It offers retail, corporate and investment banking, and through subsidiaries also insurance and asset management.
icln: iShares Global Clean Energy (ICLN) invests worldwide in solar, wind and other clean-energy companies.
icnt: Impossible Cloud Network (ICNT) is a decentralized protocol for business cloud services: storage, compute and networking. Hardware owners contribute resources and service providers use them; ICNT is needed for node collateral, access to resources and staking.
icp: Internet Computer is a blockchain from the Swiss DFINITY Foundation (Zurich), founded by Dominic Williams, launched in 2021. The network lets websites, services and AI agents run entirely on-chain without ordinary cloud servers; ICP pays for computation.
id: SPACE ID (ID) is a universal domain name service for Web3: users register and trade domains such as .bnb or .arb that replace long wallet addresses. The project was backed by Binance Labs, and ID is its governance token.
idol: MEET48 (IDOL) is a Web3 entertainment platform about virtual and real idols that combines AI, live streaming and game mechanics. Fans support their favorite performers and take part in shows, and the IDOL token serves as the ecosystem's currency.
ilv: Illuvium is an open-world Web3 game where players explore a planet, capture creatures called Illuvials and battle in an auto-battler. The project was founded by brothers Kieran and Aaron Warwick; ILV is used for governance and rewards.
imx: Immutable (IMX) is a blockchain gaming platform from Sydney, Australia, that runs the Ethereum layer-2 networks Immutable X and Immutable zkEVM. They let players trade in-game NFTs without paying gas fees; IMX is used for fees, staking and governance.
in: INFINIT is an AI-powered DeFi intelligence protocol that lets anyone discover, compare and execute DeFi opportunities through AI agents and plain-language requests instead of navigating many apps by hand. IN is the protocol's token.
inga: ING Group is a Dutch banking group headquartered in Amsterdam, formed in 1991. It serves millions of retail customers across Europe and beyond, known for its digital-first banking, and also provides wholesale banking to large companies.
init: Initia is a blockchain network that joins many optimistic rollups into one interconnected system. Developers launch their own app-specific chains that can easily talk to each other; INIT is used for staking and governance.
inj: Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK for financial apps such as exchanges, derivatives and tokenized assets. It gives developers ready-made trading modules; INJ is used for staking, governance and paying network fees.
intc: Intel is a US chipmaker based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 1968 by Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore. It is known for Core and Xeon processors for PCs and servers and is building a contract chip-manufacturing business, Intel Foundry.
intu: Intuit is a US financial software company based in Mountain View, California, founded in 1983. It makes TurboTax for filing taxes, QuickBooks accounting for small businesses, the Credit Karma personal finance app and the Mailchimp email marketing service.
io: io.net (IO) is a decentralized GPU network on Solana that pools graphics cards from data centers, mining farms and private computers into clusters for machine learning. AI engineers rent computing power for less than in regular clouds; IO is used for payments and rewards.
iost: IOST is a high-throughput blockchain platform launched in 2019 by a team backed by Sequoia and Matrix. It uses its own Proof of Believability consensus and focuses on fast, cheap decentralized apps.
iota: IOTA is an open-source blockchain project run by the Berlin-based IOTA Foundation and founded in 2015. Originally built for the Internet of Things, it now focuses on digital identity, trade data and tokenization; the IOTA token pays fees and is used for staking.
iotx: IoTeX is a blockchain platform launched in 2017 that connects real-world devices to blockchain and AI. It feeds verified data from sensors, cars and gadgets into decentralized apps and develops the DePIN sector; IOTX is the network's native coin.
iq: IQ is the token of IQ.wiki (formerly Everipedia), the largest blockchain-based encyclopedia about crypto. The project also develops AI agents through its IQ AI platform, and the token is used for governance and rewards for editors.
irys: Irys (IRYS) is a layer-1 blockchain that combines data storage with smart-contract execution, formerly known as Bundlr. It is designed for large volumes of data for AI and Web3 applications.
isp: Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest bank, formed in 2007 by the merger of Banca Intesa and Sanpaolo IMI and headquartered in Turin. It serves millions of customers in Italy and Central and Eastern Europe and runs a large insurance and asset management business.
isrg: Intuitive Surgical is a California company founded in 1995 and a pioneer of robotic surgery. Its da Vinci system lets surgeons perform minimally invasive operations with robotic arms; the company earns money from instruments and service.
ita: iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense (ITA) invests in American defence contractors and aerospace companies that build aircraft, missiles and space systems.
itochu: Itochu is a Japanese trading house based in Tokyo and Osaka, founded in 1858 as a textile merchant. It trades and invests in apparel, food, natural resources, machinery and retail, and owns the FamilyMart convenience store chain.
itub4: Itaú Unibanco is the largest private bank in Brazil and Latin America, headquartered in São Paulo and formed in 2008 by the merger of Itaú and Unibanco. It offers retail, corporate and investment banking, credit cards, insurance and asset management.
itw: Illinois Tool Works is a US industrial manufacturer based in Glenview, Illinois, founded in 1912. It runs seven businesses, from car components and welding equipment to commercial kitchen equipment, construction fasteners and polymers.
itx: Inditex is a Spanish fashion giant from Galicia founded by Amancio Ortega, owner of the chains Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius and Oysho. It is known for fast fashion: new collections reach thousands of stores worldwide within weeks.
ivv: iShares Core S&P 500 (IVV) is BlackRock's low-cost ETF on the S&P 500 index and one of the largest ETFs in the world.
iwm: iShares Russell 2000 (IWM) tracks the Russell 2000 index of small US companies. It is more sensitive to the economy and interest rates than the S&P 500.
jasmy: JasmyCoin is the token of Jasmy, a Tokyo-based Japanese company founded by former Sony executives. Jasmy builds an Internet of Things platform where users keep control of their own personal data; JASMY is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum.
jci: Johnson Controls is a global company headquartered in Cork, Ireland, whose story began in the US in 1885 when Warren Johnson invented the electric thermostat. It makes heating, ventilation and air-conditioning, fire and security systems and smart-building software.
jct: Janction is a platform for sharing resources for AI products: GPU computing power, storage and images. Users can rent or lease out these resources, and the JCT token is used for settlements in the network.
jellyjelly: Jelly-My-Jelly (JELLYJELLY) is a meme token on Solana linked to the video app JellyJelly, created by Venmo co-founder Iqram Magdon-Ismail. The token became a symbol of the app's community and trades as a meme asset.
jepi: JPMorgan Equity Premium Income (JEPI) holds S&P 500 stocks and sells options on them to pay a high monthly income, giving up part of the upside in return.
jepq: JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income (JEPQ) holds Nasdaq-100 stocks and sells options to fund monthly payouts, trading some growth for income.
jnj: Johnson & Johnson is a US healthcare company based in New Brunswick, New Jersey, founded in 1886. It develops prescription drugs for oncology, immunology and neuroscience, plus medical devices for surgery and cardiology; its consumer brands were spun off as Kenvue in 2023.
joe: JOE is the token of LFJ (formerly Trader Joe), a decentralized exchange running on Avalanche, Arbitrum and BNB Chain. The exchange is known for its Liquidity Book liquidity model; JOE is used for staking and governance.
jpm: JPMorgan Chase is the largest US bank, headquartered in New York, with roots going back to 1799. It serves millions of customers under the Chase brand and runs investment banking, asset management and payments for big companies; it is led by Jamie Dimon.
jpyc: JPY Coin (JPYC) is a Japanese yen stablecoin from Tokyo-based JPYC Inc. Each token is designed to be worth one yen and redeemable for yen, and it runs on public blockchains such as Ethereum, Polygon and Avalanche.
jst: JUST (JST) is the governance token of the JUST decentralized finance ecosystem on the TRON blockchain, linked to Justin Sun. The platform includes the JustLend lending service and stablecoin tools, and JST holders vote on protocol settings.
jto: JTO is the governance token of Jito Network, a key piece of Solana infrastructure. Jito offers liquid staking of SOL through the JitoSOL token and a modified validator client that lets validators and stakers earn extra income from MEV.
jup: Jupiter is the largest token-swap aggregator on Solana: it searches across decentralized exchanges for the best rate. It also offers perpetual futures, limit orders and new token launches; JUP is the governance token.
kag: Kinesis Silver (KAG) is a silver-backed token from the Kinesis platform: each token represents one troy ounce of investment-grade silver held in insured vaults. It can be spent, transferred or redeemed, and holders receive a share of platform fees.
kaia: Kaia is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain formed in 2024 by merging the Klaytn (from Kakao) and Finschia (from LINE) networks. It aims to bring Web3 to millions of users in Asia directly inside the KakaoTalk and LINE messengers; KAIA is its native coin.
kaio: KAIO (formerly Libre Capital) is a platform for tokenizing institutional funds: it issues on-chain shares of funds from large asset managers, opening them up to crypto investors. The project runs on networks including Hedera and has received funding from Tether; KAIO is the governance token.
kaito: KAITO is the token of Kaito, a platform that uses AI to collect and analyze crypto news, social media and discussions. Its InfoFi network rewards content creators and researchers for the attention they attract; KAITO is used for rewards, staking and governance.
kas: Kaspa is a Proof of Work cryptocurrency launched in November 2021 with no premine or presale. It uses a BlockDAG structure (the GHOSTDAG protocol), which lets blocks be created in parallel and confirms transfers very quickly.
kat: Katana is a DeFi-focused blockchain incubated by Polygon Labs and GSR, built to concentrate liquidity for trading and lending. Holders lock KAT to receive vKAT, which gives votes on how rewards and capital are directed across the network.
kau: Kinesis Gold (KAU) is a gold-backed token from the Kinesis platform: each token represents one gram of investment-grade gold held in insured vaults. Holders can spend, transfer or redeem it and receive a share of the platform's fees as a yield.
kava: Kava (KAVA) is a layer-1 blockchain that connects the Ethereum and Cosmos ecosystems and offers DeFi services that work like a decentralized bank, such as lending and stablecoins. KAVA is used for staking, fees and governance.
kcs: KuCoin Token (KCS) is the native token of KuCoin, an international crypto exchange founded in 2017. Holders get discounts on trading fees and a share of bonuses, and KCS also pays fees on the KCC network.
keep: Keep Network (KEEP) was an Ethereum project that stored and processed private data off-chain in 'keeps' protected by secure multi-party computation, and it created the bitcoin bridge tBTC. In 2022 it merged with NuCypher into Threshold Network, and KEEP can be swapped for the T token.
kekius: Kekius Maximus is a memecoin named after the joke name Elon Musk briefly used on his X profile at the end of 2024. The project is community-driven and has no function beyond the meme.
kernel: KernelDAO is an ecosystem of restaking products on Ethereum and BNB Chain: the Kelp liquid restaking protocol, Kernel infrastructure and the Gain yield vaults. The KERNEL token is used for governance and staking.
keyence: Keyence is a Japanese industrial automation company based in Osaka, founded in 1974. It develops sensors, machine vision systems, measuring instruments and microscopes, runs without its own factories, and is known for exceptionally high profitability.
kgen: KGeN is a Web3 gaming platform that builds a network of verified real players and lets game publishers reach a live audience instead of bots. The project has a strong presence in India; KGEN is the ecosystem token.
kgst: KGST is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the Kyrgyz som and fully backed by reserves. It is designed as a digital form of the som for fast, transparent payments and transfers in Kyrgyzstan and the wider Central Asian region.
kii: KiiChain (KII) is a layer-1 blockchain built for emerging markets, especially Latin America. It focuses on stablecoin payments, currency exchange and tokenizing real-world assets for local businesses.
kite: Kite is a blockchain for the "agentic economy", where AI agents can make payments on their own and securely. The network supports the x402 standard that lets machines pay for online services; KITE is its native token for staking and fees.
kkr: KKR & Co. is a global investment firm based in New York, founded in 1976 by Henry Kravis, George Roberts and Jerome Kohlberg. A pioneer of leveraged buyouts, it manages private equity, credit, infrastructure and real estate funds and owns the insurer Global Atlantic.
klac: KLA Corporation is an American maker of process-control equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, based in California. Its inspection and metrology systems find defects on silicon wafers and photomasks; its customers are the world's largest chipmakers.
kmno: Kamino is a DeFi platform on Solana that combines lending, borrowing, leverage and automated liquidity management. It began as the easiest way to earn from providing liquidity through one-click, auto-compounding strategies; KMNO is the governance token.
knc: Kyber Network Crystal (KNC) is the token of KyberSwap, a decentralized aggregator that finds the best exchange rate across many DEXs on multiple networks. Kyber Network was founded in Singapore in 2017 by Loi Luu and Victor Tran; KNC is used for governance.
kntq: Kinetiq (KNTQ) is the token of a liquid staking protocol on Hyperliquid that issues kHYPE for staked HYPE. The team also builds Markets.xyz for round-the-clock futures trading on stocks, currencies and commodities.
ko: The Coca-Cola Company is an American company from Atlanta and the world's largest maker of soft drinks; the Coca-Cola drink itself was invented in 1886. It also owns Sprite, Fanta, Dasani water and Costa Coffee, and sells its products in more than 200 countries.
koge: KOGE is a token on BNB Chain issued by 48 Club, a long-running BNB Chain community that operates validators and MEV-protection infrastructure. The token is used inside the 48 Club ecosystem and is widely traded on BNB Chain exchanges.
ksm: Kusama (KSM) is a blockchain built on the same code as Polkadot, created by Gavin Wood as a «canary network» for testing new features. Projects test upgrades here in real conditions before launching on Polkadot; KSM is used for staking and governance.
kta: Keeta (KTA) is a high-performance layer-1 blockchain designed to connect transfers across different blockchains and traditional payment systems. The project is backed by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and KTA is used to pay network fees.
kub: KUB Coin (KUB) is the native coin of KUB Chain (formerly Bitkub Chain), the blockchain created by Thailand's crypto exchange Bitkub. It is used to pay network fees, for staking and in ecosystem apps in Thailand.
kweb: KraneShares CSI China Internet (KWEB) invests in Chinese internet companies such as Alibaba, Tencent, PDD and Meituan.
kweichow-moutai: Kweichow Moutai is a Chinese state-owned maker of baijiu, a strong grain liquor, from the town of Maotai in Guizhou province. Its Moutai liquor is China's most prestigious alcoholic drink, given as a gift on holidays and served at official banquets.
la: Lagrange is a network that generates zero-knowledge proofs, letting blockchains and AI systems verify computations. Its services include a ZK coprocessor and verifiable AI; LA is used to pay for proofs and for staking.
lava: Lava Network is a protocol that gives apps, wallets and AI agents reliable access to blockchain data through a decentralized marketplace of RPC node providers across many chains. LAVA is used to pay for requests and to stake by providers.
layer: Solayer is a project in the Solana ecosystem developing InfiniSVM, a hardware-accelerated blockchain compatible with the Solana Virtual Machine. The network uses RDMA technology for ultra-fast communication between nodes; LAYER is the project's token.
lcx: LCX is a crypto exchange and blockchain company from Vaduz, Liechtenstein, registered under the country's blockchain law. It offers trading, storage and tokenization of digital assets for regulated markets in Europe, and the LCX token gives users fee discounts and access to platform services.
ldo: Lido DAO is the governance token of Lido, the largest liquid staking protocol on Ethereum, launched in 2020. Users stake ETH and receive the stETH token in return, which they can freely use in DeFi; LDO holders vote on the protocol's parameters.
leo: LEO Token is the utility token of iFinex, the owner of the Bitfinex exchange, issued in 2019. Holders get trading-fee discounts on Bitfinex, and the company regularly buys back and burns tokens.
light: Bitlight is a project from Bitlight Labs developing the RGB protocol for smart contracts and token issuance on top of Bitcoin and the Lightning Network. Its aim is to bring stablecoins and other assets to Bitcoin without a separate blockchain.
lin: Linde is the world's largest industrial gases company, formed in 2018 by the merger of Germany's Linde AG and America's Praxair. It supplies oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen and helium to hospitals, steel, chemical and electronics makers and also builds gas plants.
linea: Linea (LINEA) is an Ethereum layer-2 network built on zkEVM technology by Consensys, the company behind the MetaMask wallet. It makes transactions cheaper and faster while staying fully Ethereum-compatible, and burns part of the ETH collected in network fees.
lingo: Lingo is a gamified Web3 rewards ecosystem backed by real-world assets (RWA). Income from these assets funds regular real-world prizes and benefits for the community, regardless of token price swings; LINGO is the ecosystem token.
link: Chainlink is a decentralised oracle network that feeds smart contracts with real-world data such as prices, exchange rates and event results. Launched in 2017 under Sergey Nazarov, it uses LINK to pay node operators.
lion: Loaded Lions (LION) is the token of the flagship NFT collection of the Crypto.com exchange, featuring lion avatars. It is used within the collection's ecosystem on the Cronos network for rewards, access to events and the holders' community.
lista: Lista DAO (LISTA) is a liquid staking and lending protocol on BNB Chain. Users stake BNB and receive slisBNB, and can borrow the lisUSD stablecoin against various assets as collateral; LISTA is the governance token.
lit: LIT is the token of Lighter, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange built as a ZK rollup on Ethereum. Its standout feature is order matching and liquidations that are verifiable with cryptographic proofs, at speeds close to centralized exchanges.
lly: Eli Lilly is an American pharmaceutical company from Indianapolis, founded in 1876. It is known for insulin, the diabetes and obesity drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, and medicines in oncology and immunology, and is one of the world's largest drugmakers.
lmt: Lockheed Martin is the largest US defense contractor, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland. It builds F-35 and F-16 fighter jets, missiles, missile defense systems, Sikorsky helicopters and spacecraft, and its main customer is the US government.
lobo: LOBO•THE•WOLF•PUP (LOBO) is a meme token on Bitcoin's Runes protocol with a wolf-pup mascot. It became one of the first popular runes, and part of the fees paid at launch went to Bitcoin miners.
lon: Tokenlon is a decentralized exchange aggregator built by imToken, the crypto wallet maker. It finds swap prices across liquidity sources for Ethereum tokens, and LON is its governance and fee-sharing token.
low: Lowe's is the second-largest home improvement retailer in the US, founded in North Carolina in 1921. It sells building materials, tools, appliances and garden products and offers installation services.
lpt: Livepeer (LPT) is a decentralized network for processing and transcoding video, launched in 2017. Node operators provide GPU power to re-encode streams and, more recently, to generate AI video; LPT is staked to distribute work and earn rewards.
lqty: Liquity is a decentralized lending protocol on Ethereum where users borrow the LUSD stablecoin, or BOLD in version two, against ETH collateral. The protocol runs without administrators; LQTY is staked to earn a share of fees.
lrc: Loopring is a decentralised exchange protocol on an Ethereum layer-2 zkRollup, founded in 2017 by Daniel Wang, offering both order-book and AMM trading with lower fees than the main chain. LRC is its token, used for staking and protocol incentives.
lrcx: Lam Research is a US maker of chip-manufacturing equipment based in Fremont, California, founded in 1980. Its tools etch and deposit thin layers of material on silicon wafers; customers include the largest memory and processor makers.
lsk: Lisk (LSK) is a project founded in Berlin in 2016 that now operates as a layer-2 network on Ethereum. It builds financial infrastructure for businesses to store, transfer and invest money in fiat currencies and stablecoins.
ltc: Litecoin is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies, created in 2011 by former Google engineer Charlie Lee from bitcoin's code. Blocks arrive four times faster than bitcoin's, which is why it is often called 'silver to bitcoin's gold'.
lumia: Lumia is a blockchain for tokenizing real-world assets that emerged from the rebrand of Orion Protocol. The network makes it easier to issue and trade tokenized assets, and LUMIA is used for fees and staking.
luna: Terra (LUNA) is the native token of the new Terra blockchain, created in 2022 after the collapse of the algorithmic stablecoin UST. The old network was renamed Terra Classic (LUNC), while the new one runs on the Cosmos SDK and uses LUNA for staking and governance.
lunc: Terra Luna Classic is the original Terra blockchain left after the collapse of the UST stablecoin in May 2022. The community then launched a new Terra 2.0 network, while the old chain and its LUNC coin live on under community governance that burns tokens.
lyx: LUKSO is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain built for creators, fashion and culture. It was founded by Fabian Vogelsteller, author of the ERC-20 token standard, and offers Universal Profiles, smart accounts that act as a person's on-chain identity.
m: MemeCore is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for meme coins. The project aims to turn memes from pure speculation into a tool for culture and communities: anyone can launch tokens and earn rewards for helping them grow popular.
ma: Mastercard is a US payments company headquartered in Purchase, New York, and one of the world's two biggest card networks alongside Visa. It runs the network behind Mastercard, Maestro and Cirrus cards, connecting banks, merchants and cardholders; it does not issue cards or lend money itself.
mag7xon: Ondo Magnificent 7 and Crypto Portfolio (MAG7XON) is a tokenized portfolio from Ondo Finance that combines shares of the 'Magnificent Seven' US tech giants (Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Tesla) with a slice of cryptocurrencies.
magic: Treasure (MAGIC) is a decentralized gaming ecosystem that grew up on the Arbitrum network. Treasure builds games and AI-powered entertainment products, and MAGIC is its native token for payments and rewards.
magma: Magma Finance is a decentralized exchange on the Sui blockchain. It uses concentrated and adaptive liquidity so traders get better prices and liquidity providers earn more fees; the MAGMA token is used for governance and rewards.
mana: Decentraland (MANA) is a virtual world on Ethereum, opened to the public in 2020, where users buy plots of LAND as NFTs, build scenes, host events and sell digital items. MANA is the in-world currency and the voting token of its DAO.
manta: Manta Network is an ecosystem built around Manta Pacific, an Ethereum layer-2 network that uses zero-knowledge proofs. It makes it easier to build apps with ZK technology and low fees; MANTA is used for staking and governance.
mantra: MANTRA is a layer-1 blockchain for tokenizing real-world assets (RWA) such as real estate, with a focus on regulatory compliance. The project holds a license in the UAE, and MANTRA is used for staking, fees and governance.
mar: Marriott International is the world's largest hotel company by number of rooms, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland, and founded in 1927. Its brands include Marriott, Ritz-Carlton, Sheraton, Westin, W Hotels and more than 30 others.
marscoin: MARSCOIN is a token on BNB Chain conceived as a crypto asset paired with a company's stock. It is a speculative meme project with no standalone product, so its price depends on community interest.
mask: Mask Network (MASK) is a project that connects ordinary social networks with Web3: its browser extension lets people encrypt messages and send cryptocurrency and NFTs directly inside Twitter (X). MASK serves as the governance token.
mav: Maverick Protocol is DeFi infrastructure built around Maverick AMM, a decentralised exchange whose liquidity can move automatically with the price, so liquidity providers need less manual rebalancing. MAV is its governance and incentive token.
mbg-token: MBG is the token of MultiBank Group, one of the large forex and derivatives brokers, founded in 2005. The token is used within the group's ecosystem for trading discounts, staking and access to tokenized assets.
mbl: MovieBloc is a blockchain platform for film distribution that aims to break the dominance of big studios and cinema chains. Creators get a transparent revenue share and audience data, while viewers earn MBL tokens for curating, subtitling and promoting films.
mc: LVMH is the world's largest luxury goods group, based in Paris and formed in 1987 by the merger of Moët Hennessy and Louis Vuitton. It controls more than 70 houses, including Louis Vuitton, Dior, Tiffany, Bulgari, Sephora, Moët & Chandon champagne and Hennessy cognac; it is led by Bernard Arnault.
mcd: McDonald's is the world's largest fast-food restaurant chain, headquartered in Chicago, built up from 1955 by Ray Kroc. Most of its restaurants are run by franchisees, and the company earns mainly from rent and royalties paid by them.
mck: McKesson is the largest pharmaceutical distributor in the US, headquartered in Irving, Texas, and founded in 1833. It supplies medicines and medical products to pharmacies and hospitals and provides technology for prescriptions and cancer clinics.
mco: Moody's Corporation is a US financial information company based in New York, founded by John Moody in 1909. Moody's Investors Service is one of the three big credit rating agencies rating bonds of companies and governments, and Moody's Analytics sells risk data and software.
mdlz: Mondelez International is a US snack food company based in Chicago, created in 2012 when Kraft Foods split. It makes some of the world's best-known snacks, including Oreo, Milka, Cadbury, Toblerone, Ritz, belVita and Halls.
mdt: Medtronic is one of the world's largest medical device makers, founded in Minneapolis in 1949 and legally domiciled in Ireland. It makes pacemakers, insulin pumps, surgical and neurostimulation equipment for hospitals in more than 150 countries.
me: Magic Eden is one of the largest NFT marketplaces, founded in 2021 in the Solana ecosystem. It lets people buy and sell NFTs, Ordinals and Runes on Bitcoin, Solana, Ethereum, Base and other networks; the ME token is used for governance and rewards.
med: MediBloc is a South Korean healthcare blockchain project that lets patients store and share their medical records securely. MED is the native token of its Panacea blockchain, built with the Cosmos SDK, and is used for fees and staking.
mediatek: MediaTek is a Taiwanese chip designer based in Hsinchu, founded in 1997. It designs Dimensity and Helio processors for Android smartphones as well as chips for TVs, Wi-Fi routers, tablets and smart devices; it has no factories of its own.
mega: MegaETH (MEGA) is an Ethereum layer-2 network marketed as a «real-time blockchain» with millisecond latency and very high throughput. It stays Ethereum-compatible, so apps can run almost instantly without changing their tools.
melania: Melania Meme (MELANIA) is a memecoin on the Solana network launched in January 2025 in Melania Trump's name. The token is presented as a digital collectible and a sign of support, with no practical function or ownership rights.
meme: Memecoin (MEME) is the token of Memeland, a project created by the team behind the popular entertainment site 9GAG. It serves as a 'coin of meme culture' for the community and Memeland's NFT collections and does not claim a technical function of its own.
merl: Merlin Chain (MERL) is a bitcoin layer-2 network based on ZK-rollup technology, launched in 2024. It lets users move BTC, Runes and BRC-20 tokens into an environment with cheap transactions and DeFi apps; MERL is the network's governance token.
met-token: Meteora is a liquidity platform on Solana with dynamic pools and a DLMM mechanism, where trading fees change with market volatility. Many new Solana tokens and memecoins launch and trade through Meteora; MET is the project's governance token.
meta: Meta Platforms is a US company from Menlo Park, California, founded by Mark Zuckerberg in 2004 as Facebook. It owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, earns mostly from advertising, and develops Llama AI, smart glasses and Quest VR headsets.
meta-token: MetaDAO is a fundraising and governance platform on Solana that uses futarchy: decisions are made by market prices rather than direct votes, as traders bet on whether a proposal will raise or lower the token's value. META is its token.
metal: Metal Blockchain (METAL) is a layer-0 blockchain from Metallicus built on Avalanche's consensus technology. It targets payments and financial services for banks and is linked to the Metal Pay digital banking app; METAL is used for fees and staking.
metis: Metis is an Ethereum layer-2 network based on optimistic rollups and the first to launch a decentralized sequencer. It promises fast, cheap transactions for DeFi and games; METIS is used for fees and staking.
mew: cat in a dogs world (MEW) is a Solana meme token whose idea is a "cat in a world of dogs" – a challenge to the many dog-themed meme coins. It runs purely on its community's meme culture.
mey: Mey Network is a blockchain ecosystem for tokenizing real-world assets (RWA). It consists of Meychain, a dedicated layer-1 blockchain for RWAs, and the MeyFi platform, while the MEY token is used for fees and network operations.
mgo: Mango Network is a layer-1 blockchain with a multi-virtual-machine, omnichain design that supports MoveVM, EVM and SVM, so developers from different ecosystems can build on one network. MGO is its native token for fees and staking.
midea-group: Midea Group is a Chinese home appliance maker from Foshan, Guangdong, founded in 1968 by He Xiangjian. It makes air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines and small appliances, and owns German robot maker KUKA and Toshiba's home appliance business.
mimatic: MAI is a dollar stablecoin from QiDao (Mai Finance), a lending protocol that started on Polygon. Users borrow MAI by locking crypto such as ETH or MATIC in over-collateralized vaults, and the protocol keeps MAI close to one US dollar.
mina: Mina Protocol (MINA) is a blockchain whose size stays at about 22 kilobytes thanks to recursive zero-knowledge proofs. That lets anyone verify the network even from a smartphone; MINA is used for fees and staking.
mira: Mira is a decentralized network for verifying AI output: it breaks AI-generated content into individual claims and checks them by consensus across several AI models, reducing the need for human review. Apps such as the Klok chat run on it.
mitsubishi-corp: Mitsubishi Corporation is Japan's largest trading house (sogo shosha), based in Tokyo. It invests and trades worldwide in energy, metals and mining, food, chemicals, cars and infrastructure, and is one of Berkshire Hathaway's holdings.
mitsubishi-ufj: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) is Japan's largest banking group, headquartered in Tokyo. It provides retail, corporate and investment banking, asset management and brokerage services, and owns a large stake in the US bank Morgan Stanley.
mitsui-co: Mitsui & Co. is one of Japan's largest general trading companies (sogo shosha), based in Tokyo, with roots in the Mitsui group dating to the 17th century. It invests in and trades energy, iron ore and metals, chemicals, food, infrastructure and healthcare worldwide; Berkshire Hathaway is a major shareholder.
mizuho-fg: Mizuho Financial Group is a Japanese banking group based in Tokyo, created in 2000 through the merger of three banks. It provides banking, trust, brokerage and investment banking services to corporations, governments and individual clients.
mlk-token: MiL.k is a South Korean blockchain platform that connects loyalty programs of different companies, including airlines, hotels and shops. Users exchange loyalty points through the MLK token and spend them with partners.
mmm: 3M is a US industrial conglomerate from St. Paul, Minnesota, founded in 1902 as Minnesota Mining and Manufacturing. Known for Post-it notes and Scotch tape, it makes thousands of products, from abrasives and adhesives to safety gear and electronics materials.
mmt: Momentum is a decentralized exchange with concentrated liquidity on the Sui network. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity, while MMT is used for governance and rewards for protocol participants.
mnde: Marinade is a liquid staking protocol on Solana: users stake SOL and receive mSOL, a token that keeps earning staking rewards while it can still be traded or used in DeFi. MNDE is Marinade's governance token.
mnst: Monster Beverage is a US drinks company based in Corona, California, best known for Monster Energy, one of the world's top-selling energy drinks. It also sells Reign, Bang and other brands, with bottling and distribution largely handled by Coca-Cola's network.
mnt: Mantle is a layer-2 network for Ethereum that grew out of BitDAO and is closely linked to the Bybit crypto exchange. It lowers transaction costs for DeFi apps; MNT pays fees and is used for voting in the ecosystem.
mo: Altria is a US tobacco company based in Richmond, Virginia, formerly known as Philip Morris Companies. It sells Marlboro cigarettes, Black & Mild cigars, smokeless tobacco and on! nicotine pouches in the US and owns a stake in the brewing giant AB InBev.
moca: Moca Network (MOCA) is digital identity infrastructure from Animoca Brands: one universal account for a person's assets, identity and reputation across different blockchains. The project grew out of the Mocaverse NFT collection, and MOCA is used across its ecosystem.
mog: Mog Coin (MOG) is a meme token on Ethereum launched in 2023, inspired by the internet slang word mog, meaning to outshine someone. It runs on the community's viral meme culture and has no separate product.
mon: Monad is a high-performance Layer 1 blockchain that is fully compatible with Ethereum (EVM) and executes transactions in parallel for speed and low fees. Its mainnet launched in November 2025; MON pays network fees and is used for staking.
moodeng: Moo Deng (MOODENG) is a Solana meme token dedicated to Moo Deng, the pygmy hippo from Thailand's Khao Kheow Open Zoo who became an internet star in 2024. The token has no product of its own.
morpho: Morpho is a decentralized lending protocol on Ethereum, Base and other networks where users deposit assets to earn interest or borrow against collateral. It lets anyone create separate isolated markets and vaults; MORPHO is the governance token.
move: Movement is a blockchain network that brings the Move programming language to developers, including in the Ethereum ecosystem. Move was created at Meta for the Diem project and focuses on smart-contract safety; MOVE is the network's token.
movr: Moonriver is a fully Ethereum-compatible smart contract parachain on Kusama and the sister network of Moonbeam in the Polkadot ecosystem. It serves as a place to launch and test new dApps; MOVR pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
mpc: Marathon Petroleum is a US oil refiner from Findlay, Ohio, one of the largest in the country, spun off from Marathon Oil in 2011. It runs a network of refineries that make gasoline, diesel and jet fuel and controls the pipeline company MPLX.
mplx: Metaplex (MPLX) is the leading tokenization platform on Solana: its standards and tools are used to create most NFTs and many tokens on that network. MPLX is the protocol's governance token.
mrk: Merck & Co. (known as MSD outside the US and Canada) is an American pharmaceutical company from New Jersey with roots going back to 1891. It makes the cancer drug Keytruda, the HPV vaccine Gardasil and medicines for animals.
mrna: Moderna is a US biotech company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, founded in 2010, that develops medicines based on messenger RNA (mRNA). It is best known for its Spikevax COVID-19 vaccine and also sells an RSV vaccine, mRESVIA, while developing vaccines and cancer treatments.
mrsh: Marsh McLennan is a US professional services firm from New York and the world's largest insurance broker, founded in 1871. It brings together Marsh (insurance), Guy Carpenter (reinsurance), Mercer (HR consulting) and Oliver Wyman (management consulting).
mrvl: Marvell Technology is an American designer of semiconductors for data infrastructure, founded in 1995. It makes chips for data centres, networking, storage and cars, including custom AI processors built for the big cloud companies.
ms: Morgan Stanley is a US investment bank headquartered in New York, founded in 1935. It manages wealth for affluent clients, trades securities and advises on mergers and acquisitions; it also owns the E*Trade brokerage platform.
msft: Microsoft is a US technology company based in Redmond, Washington, founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen. It develops Windows, Office, the Azure cloud, LinkedIn, Xbox and the Copilot assistant, and is a key partner of OpenAI.
